title: Design Diary #2 - A Land in Peril / Artist Reveal / Discussing Challenges / Player Questions
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EIKIx9Xpl7c

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns with two reveals: the game is called *A Land in Peril — The Adventure Game*, and the artist is Craig Price (Craig Lighthouse) of *Devoured*, whose stark black-and-white work he shows across a cover mock-up, the magic user, a bone-armoured warrior, and the quadrant map.

The episode's best material is the application of the lesson from Diary #1 — don't patch, go back. Originally each turn's milestone made the boss stronger, which made the six bosses nearly impossible to design. Rather than patching, he asked what the milestone was actually *for*: time pressure. So now a milestone destroys a random quest location instead. It creates the pressure, reinforces the title, punishes players who linger in a doomed dungeon, and leaves the bosses designable. Similarly, weapon enchantments no longer shift difficulty — they add or remove dice.

He then details the challenge types (combat, stat, adventure, escape, boss), the press-your-luck locking system that banks successes across turns, and the determination stat that doubles as hit points and currency. Player questions close it out: roughly a year to completion, likely Game Crafter, no scripted campaign — ever.

----

Does destroying map locations as a timer appeal more than a boss that simply scales up?
